result.title: Ideas on the Move: Soichi Noguchi
result.description:
"Don't let ambition become self-sacrifice”

@astrosoichi on what space taught him about ambition, limits, and readjusting to life on the ground - which he says was the hardest part.

As an overachiever, he says, you push to do more than you can handle. Eventually something gives, be it your health, your relationships, or your daily life. 

His advice to the next generation: don't let that something be you.

result.title: How air bubbles can remove 99.9% of forever chemicals from water
result.description:
‘Forever chemicals’ are found in masses of products, from non-stick pans to clothing. As their nickname suggests, these per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are hard to get rid of. 

US company Allonnia provides a solution to remove PFAS from water using air. As bubbles rise, they separate out more than 99.99% of PFAS molecules.

PFAS destruction technologies have been selected as one of the World Economic Forum’s Top 10 Emerging Technologies of 2026.

result.title: Ideas on the Move: Asma Khan
result.description:
"Without the ingredients, we would be nothing."

Author and restaurateur Asma Khan says success on the food scene shouldn’t mean putting chefs on a pedestal, but instead recognizing the people who make every meal possible.

Joining us in Dalian, China for #AMNC26, the founder of Darjeeling Express discussed how she wants her own journey to inspire hope in others - from starting as a Muslim immigrant in her forties to creating one of London's most celebrated restaurants.

Today, she's calling for greater recognition of farmers, and emphasises the importance of the healthy soils and food systems which are vital for making nutritious, high-quality food accessible to everyone.

#IdeasOnTheMove #FoodSystems

result.title: There are now 80 machines for every human online
result.description:
Non-human identities, from bots to AI agents to Internet of Things devices, now massively outnumber people online. 

Many of these NHIs have authorization to carry out tasks on behalf of human users. But has security kept up with the pace of these new capabilities? Helmut Reisinger of @paloaltontwks discusses the challenge.

In the Global Cybersecurity Outlook 2026, 87% of leaders surveyed identified AI-related vulnerabilities as the fastest-growing cyber risk.

result.title: Your home could be powered by an electric car
result.description:
In the evening, power grids are under strain as millions of people switch on lights, appliances and air conditioners.
 
Meanwhile, fully charged electric cars sit idle, holding power that the grid needs.
 
A new technology called everything-to-grid energy is addressing this gap. It can turn vehicles, buildings and factories into nodes in a flexible, intelligent network that shares power with wherever it’s most needed. Electric vehicle owners receive money, utility bill credits or reduced financing costs in return. In developing regions, the technology could allow fleets of e-bikes or even agricultural tools to act as back-up power sources for the whole community.
 
Everything-to-grid has been selected as one of the World Economic Forum’s Top 10 Emerging Technologies of 2026.
